Assessing the effectiveness of climate-smart health facilities in small island Caribbean nations (Ann Glob Health 2025)

dedupe_keys.name: paho who smart hospitals initiative climate smart retrofits of caribbean health facilities

description: The Smart Hospitals initiative of the Pan American Health Organization retrofits health facilities in Caribbean small island states so that they keep working through hurricanes and floods while using less energy. Building on the earlier Safe Hospitals programme, it strengthens structural and operational safety and adds green technology such as solar panels, battery storage and efficient electrical systems, giving facilities energy autonomy during emergencies. The provider is PAHO/WHO in partnership with the UK Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office, and an independent evaluation by Lichtveld and colleagues appeared in Annals of Global Health (2025). Coverage starts with pilots in 2012 in Saint Vincent and the Grenadines and Saint Kitts and Nevis; the evaluation covers 55 retrofitted facilities in seven countries and finds statistically significant improvements in Hospital Safety Index scores, with effectiveness depending on local money and staff to maintain the work. PAHO reports that Georgetown Hospital in Saint Vincent stayed functional when a storm damaged 39 clinics, and that all four smart facilities in Jamaica kept working after Hurricane Melissa in 2025. The PAHO page offers a free toolkit, dashboard and case studies; the article is open access under CC BY. Caveats: outcome claims on the PAHO page are programme reports, and the evaluation relies on secondary data. Simulation uses: parameters for backup power and functionality of retrofitted facilities in storm scenarios. Related records: the New Orleans Veterans Affairs rebuild (case_study-new-orleans-va-hospital-flood-resilient-rebuild) is another hospital design response.
